title: The 20 Percent Plan Changes Shape. Oil Prices Remain Unsettled
part1:
This news has two parts: a policy plan that changed quickly, and an unsettled market. A big number made the headlines, then the next day it took the form of a different deal. Even so, oil prices did not calm down right away.

On July 13, President Trump put forward a plan to charge 20 percent on all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz. He said it would help cover the cost of the United States keeping the strait safe. But this was only a proposal. The fee had not begun to be collected.

The figure of 20 percent stood out. But there was no detailed explanation of how it would become an actual charge: who would pay, what the amount would be based on, or how it would be collected. No plan for how the system would work was shown. The headline was striking, but the system was still unclear. That was the proposal.
part2:
Then, on July 14, Trump announced that he was withdrawing the fee proposal and replacing it with trade and investment deals that Gulf countries would make with the United States. He said the decision was based on talks with Middle Eastern leaders. The headline changed from a fee plan to trade and investment deals.

One might have thought the market would catch its breath too, but the story did not end there. After the announcement, Brent crude futures, an international benchmark, briefly gave back some of their gains. But soon they returned to a level close to where they had been before the announcement. At the time of the report, they were above $85 a barrel, up about 2.6 percent.
part3:
This price move alone does not show that the market felt reassured by the withdrawal, or that the proposal meant nothing. At the time, attacks by the United States and Iran and a sea blockade continued, and concerns about tanker safety remained. The fee plan being withdrawn did not mean that concerns about ship safety had gone away. Nor can this price move alone tell us how replacing the plan with trade and investment deals affected ship safety.

The main story in the headlines changed in just one day. Even so, concerns at sea continued at that point. Looking at the policy statements alongside the market moves shows that changing the plan alone did not bring the news story to a close.
in_one_line: Trump replaced his proposed Hormuz shipping fee with trade and investment deals, but oil prices remained unsettled.
